findings.title: Federated exhausted recovery credential is removed with local-storage API
findings.body: After switching to RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential, optUserCredentialFound can be a federated credential. When allCodesUsed is true, this line calls authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId()). That API removes credentials from Keycloak's local credential store, not from the user-storage provider that owns the federated credential. Federated credential models may also have no local persistent ID (for example the test provider returns a model built via createFromValues without copying the stored ID). As a result, after the last recovery code the exhausted federated credential is not removed, or the call fails for a null ID, leaving the credential lifecycle broken. This path is not covered by the added test because it only uses the first code.

findings.title: Recovery codes are not consumed by the test user storage provider
findings.body: The new recovery-code validation branch only checks whether the submitted code is present in the stored list and returns true. It never removes the matched code or persists a reduced list, so recovery codes remain reusable indefinitely in this test provider. Consequently the added test does not exercise one-time-use behavior or the all-codes-used removal path in RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator. The provider should consume/update the verified code, or a test should cover reuse and exhaustion.
